title: Count orders for every customer
prompt: For every customer, return first_name and orders, the number of orders they have placed. A customer who has never ordered shows 0. Put the most orders first, and sort customers with the same number by first_name.
hints: Which join keeps a customer who has no orders, and what does that customer's row hold?
Count something that is NULL when there was no order.
LEFT JOIN orders AS o ON o.customer_id = c.id ... count(o.id) AS orders

wrongAnswers.misconception: Counts joined rows, so a customer with no orders shows 1.
Uses an inner join, which leaves out customers with no orders.

feedback: Check two things: all 20 customers appear, and the ones who never ordered show 0.
